To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have analytically derived the energy-bandwidth limits for electro-optic (E/O) modulators and demonstrated that the energy per bit can be reduced by two orders of magnitude by using coupling modulation.

(i) the energy-bandwidth product of electro-optic (EO) modulators is fundamentally limited by the energy-bandwidth of the cavity, which can be increased by using multiple resonances, (ii) the energy-band-width limit of a single resonance EO modulator can be broken by using coupling modulation, (iii) a dual cavity modulators can simultaneously achieve a high bandwidth (80GHz) and low energy-per-bit (26 aJ/bit) by using both index and coupling modulation.

1) we have derived the fundamental energy-bandwidth trade-off limit for intra-cavity electro-optic modulator; 2) we have proposed a novel dual cavity modulator that breaks this energy-bandwidth limit; 3) we have experimentally verified that this dual cavity modulator can achieve a record high 3 dB modulation bandwidth of 80 GHz and ultra-low energy per bit of 0.26 a Joule.

we have shown how to overcome the energy-bandwidth tradeoff of modulators, and how to design modulators that can simultaneously achieve ultra-low energy-per-bits and ultra-high bandwidths.

the energy-bandwidth product can be decoupled in electro-optic modulator design.
